Elect Peter Beardmore as vice chair of the Finance Committee

Approve minutes of the Finance Committee (5/28, 6/11) and tri-board meetings (1/12, 1/27, 3/10)

budget_items.topic: FY27 state aid / cherry sheet changes, school-related
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair compared the FY27 governor's request (basis for the town budget) to the final cherry sheet signed July 9 by Governor Healey, showing net increases across school-related receipts and charges.
Chapter 70 aid rose from the governor's request to the final signed budget.
No change was reported between the governor's request and the final figure.
This line increased between the request and the final budget.

budget_items.topic: Town-wide net cherry sheet increase (all departments)
budget_items.what_was_said: A member reported hearing the overall town-wide net increase between the governor's request and final budget, separate from the school-only figure.
UGGA increased as part of the town-side cherry sheet changes.
This line also increased on the town side.

budget_items.topic: Superintendent's requested items funded by state aid increase
budget_items.what_was_said: Five items were requested: a primary school reading specialist, a Turkey Hill reading specialist, raising the Lunenburg vice principal to full-time, 52 Ignite tutoring seats, and moving the high school music teacher to full-time for the second half of the year.

budget_items.topic: Cost of restoring grade 1-4 sections vs. superintendent's plan
budget_items.what_was_said: A member asked why the money wasn't used to restore elementary sections to reduce class size; the answer given was that a fully loaded teacher costs over a certain amount and would not cover all needs, and the reading specialist/Ignite option was considered a better use.
Recurring buyouts and a high-deductible/HSA option produced savings; the superintendent was reportedly comfortable funding the primary reading specialist from these savings for FY27.
The chair noted this reserve remains available during the year for unanticipated needs, calling it a risk-management tool.

budget_items.topic: School department budget shortfall relative to level services
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said the school department had to cut its operations by a stated amount to fit within its FY27 allocation, and that even with the new state aid the district would still be short next year.

budget_items.topic: Green Communities grant request (Mass Save/National Grid)
budget_items.what_was_said: The green committee is trying to assemble enough shovel-ready projects (via CBAs) to justify a grant request, aiming for the maximum award.
The last portion of a prior green grant award was received near the end of the fiscal year after project completion.
The comprehensive building assessment estimated the cost to replace all windows at Turkey Hill.
Rebates are available for residents and for the town buying electric mowers, with a cost comparison between electric and gas zero-turn mowers given.
Rebates are paid per ton of heat pump capacity installed; described using the primary school installation as an example.
Rebate is based on square footage times number of temperature 'sequences' programmed, up to a stated maximum number of sequences.
figures_as_heard: 5 cents or 10 cents times the square feet
a buck 30 times the square footage

budget_items.topic: ADA compliance trigger tied to building investment at Turkey Hill
budget_items.what_was_said: A formula based on assessed value means spending above a fraction of that value on the building could trigger a mandate for full ADA compliance; figures given were approximate.

budget_items.topic: MSBA Accelerated Repair Program state budget
budget_items.what_was_said: This statewide program funding window (windows/roof) recycles every two years and has a stated total budget.

budget_items.topic: Heat pump conversion cost per square foot
budget_items.what_was_said: Estimated conversion costs vary widely depending on existing building systems.
Residential and municipal buildings can earn payments for curtailing electricity use during peak summer events.

decisions.decision: The committee will remain in its current seating/liaison configuration for this meeting.
Reported that the superintendent is comfortable funding the primary school reading specialist position out of health insurance savings for FY27.
The Finance Committee's capital planning committee representative slot was left undecided; the topic was tabled for a future meeting.
Peter Beardmore agreed to serve as the Finance Committee liaison to the School Committee.
Rather than formally assign department liaisons for police, facilities, DPW and fire, Peter Beardmore (as vice chair) will serve as an informal inbound point of contact for those departments.

Department head and school budget preview presentations to the Finance Committee (previously done jointly with the tri-board) will move to a November/December timeframe going forward, ahead of the formal budget season.
The next two Finance Committee meetings will be focused primarily on the additional special town meeting and its warrant articles.

The August 13 meeting is expected to feature a presentation from the school committee, superintendent, and petitioner Mandy Gilman; the public hearing on the article is set for August 27, separate from that presentation meeting.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Finance Committee reorganized (re-electing Chris Manard as chair, electing Peter Beardmore vice chair and Tom Gray clerk), heard a presentation from the Green Communities Committee on Mass Save incentive programs for municipal and school buildings, and reviewed the FY27 state aid ("cherry sheet") changes and the superintendent's proposed use of the resulting funds plus health insurance savings. The committee also worked through committee and liaison assignments for the coming year, deferring a decision on the capital planning committee seat, and set a schedule leading up to an additional special town meeting expected before September 3.
